newsitem.title: JORDAN: Foreign demand for Jordan shares but index falls.
newsitem.headline: Foreign demand for Jordan shares but index falls.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell 0.27 percent on Saturday, but foreign and local demand for blue chips kept turnover busy.

Brokers said Arab Potash was the main focus of foreign buying, though international demand failed to lift stock in the majority state-owned company which fell 0.07 dinars to 6.62 dinars in trade worth 378,000 dinars ($533,000).
Stocks in another blue-chip firm, Jordan Cement Factories, saw even higher turnover but brokers said that included a block transfer of shares. Jordan Cement also fell back 0.01 dinars to 4.02 dinars.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.27 percent to 158.59 points in turnover of 1.61 million dinars.

Despite Saturday's fall, brokers said foreign interest in the bourse was picking up. A wave of fund buying in late May sent the official index up by eight percent but turnover has slackened since then.
"Foreign equity investment will be picking up from today's purchases and we will witness increased demand by foreigners," said Ziad al-Basha, securities manager at British Bank of the Middle East.
Basha estimated one third of Saturday's turnover came from foreign investors and said the Amman bourse was benefiting from a transfer of funds out of stocks in Egypt and Israel.
But overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 21 to six, while shares in another 14 companies were traded but closed unchanged.
"There's plenty of demand for the handful of blue-chip shares but the smaller shares are suffering," said analyst Mohammad Abdullah of Pearl Consulting.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.29 percent to 81.10 points, 2.74 percent down from the start of the year.
